transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I’m here because nobody seems to take it seriously that people at work are secretly targeting my projects, even when I show them the evidence. It is incredibly frustrating because everyone else just acts like nothing is happening.
Do you feel like people in other areas of your life, such as family members or close friends, are also acting against you or cannot be trusted?

No, not at all, this is strictly happening at work with that one competing tech team. My personal life is completely normal, and I still trust my family and friends, like my cousin who I regularly meet up with for pho on weekends.
Apart from these issues at work, have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people cannot hear or see?
No, absolutely not. I have never heard any voices or seen things that aren't really there. My senses are completely normal.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being broadcast out loud so others can hear them, or that some outside force is putting thoughts into your head?
No, I have never felt like my thoughts were being broadcast out loud for others to hear. I've also never experienced any outside force putting thoughts into my head. My mind is completely my own.
How long have you been experiencing these issues with the competing tech team targeting your projects?

This has been going on for about nine months now. It started during that big cloud migration project last year when the outages began, which is when I first realized the other team was targeting my work.
During these past nine months, have you experienced any periods of feeling constantly down, depressed, or on the contrary, unusually energetic and active?

No, I haven't experienced any periods of feeling deeply depressed or unusually energetic. Mostly, I've just been highly stressed and anxious because of how much focus it takes to protect my work from being sabotaged. It's exhausting, but my overall mood hasn't been swinging up or down like that.

The delusion is well-systematized and circumscribed to the workplace, with preserved functioning in other areas of life. This meets all ICD-10 criteria for Delusional Disorder (F22.0), allowing us to make a final diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a circumscribed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion involving a competing work team sabotaging their projects. This belief has persisted for 9 months, satisfying the duration criterion of at least 3 months. The patient exhibits no hallucinations, no passivity phenomena (such as thought insertion or broadcasting), and no history of mood episodes. Aside from the impact of this delusion at work, the patient's psychosocial functioning (e.g., relationships with family and friends) remains intact, which is characteristic of Delusional Disorder (F22.0).
